name: ABQ Coors
description: Flix Brewhouse's original Albuquerque location, near the Hinkle Family Fun Center off Coors Blvd. Full bar with house-brewed beer, reserved seating, and food ordered via QR code or a seat-side call button, with the chain's automatic 18%+ gratuity added regardless of service. Reviews are more mixed here than at most Flix locations — friendly staff and good food come up often, but so do specific complaints about slow drink refills and long waits between courses. One reviewer notes on-site security as a plus. Expect around $40+ per person for a full dinner and drinks.

name: ABQ Tramway
description: Flix Brewhouse's second Albuquerque location, off Tramway Blvd near Indian School Road. Reviewers note recent seat upgrades to sturdier recliners with working cup holders, an improvement they call out over the older Coors location nearby. Full bar and made-to-order food are delivered to reserved recliner seating via call button or QR-code order, with the standard 18%+ gratuity added automatically. Service is generally praised as attentive, though a few reviews mention slow ticket-taking and unresponsive call buttons on busier nights.

name: Carmel
description: Flix Brewhouse's Indianapolis-area location in Carmel. Full bar with a rotating house-brewed beer list, reserved seating, and food ordered via QR code or through a server, plus the chain-wide automatic 18%+ gratuity. Reviews are largely positive on food and staff friendliness, though at least one visitor found the space less clean than expected and the mobile ordering flow clunky on a first visit. Standard dinner-and-a-show pricing — plan on $50-60+ for two with food and drinks.

name: Des Moines
description: Flix Brewhouse's Des Moines location, a longtime local favorite among reviewers who describe consistently friendly staff over several years of visits. House-brewed beer and a full kitchen menu — wings, cheese curds, fried pickles — are ordered via app or server and delivered to your seat, with an automatic 18%+ gratuity built in. A few reviewers note the location doesn't proactively offer silverware or water refills unless asked. Discount member screenings and brunch events come up often in reviews as a draw.

name: El Paso East
description: One of three Flix Brewhouse locations in El Paso, occupying a former Alamo Drafthouse space. Full bar and food are ordered via server or QR code and delivered to reserved seating, with the usual automatic 18%+ gratuity. Reviews are uniformly positive and consistently call out fast, attentive table service by name — a recurring theme across recent visits — with milkshakes and buffalo mac and cheese frequently recommended.

name: Montecillo
description: The Montecillo-area location, one of three Flix Brewhouse theaters in El Paso, also a former Alamo Drafthouse space with similar interior styling. Full bar, reserved seating, and food delivered by server or via QR-code order, plus the chain's automatic 18%+ gratuity. Reviews are strongly positive and specifically praise individual servers for attentiveness — a more consistent pattern here than complaints about food or price.

name: West Towne
description: The West Towne Marketplace location, the third of Flix Brewhouse's three El Paso theaters, with an outdoor patio in addition to the standard full bar and indoor reserved seating. Food and drinks are ordered via QR code or server with the automatic 18%+ gratuity applied. Reviews are more mixed than the chain's other El Paso locations — several reviewers praise the comfortable seats and fast service, but there are specific complaints about a bland Cajun pasta dish and one report of rushed, disorganized food delivery.

name: Frisco/Little Elm
description: Flix Brewhouse's Dallas-Fort Worth-area location serving the Frisco/Little Elm corridor, with an on-site brewery, full bar, and reserved recliner seating. Food and drinks are ordered via phone/app and delivered by a server, plus the standard automatic 18%+ gratuity. Reviews are consistently positive about the beer selection and staff friendliness; the most common critique is that food and drinks can arrive separately rather than together, and service can slow down on quiet nights despite low occupancy.

name: Katy
description: Flix Brewhouse's Katy location, recently under new ownership with upgraded seating reviewers describe as more comfortable than before. Full bar with house-brewed beer, reserved seating, and food ordered via QR code and delivered by staff, with the chain's automatic 18%+ gratuity — several reviewers specifically say they're not fans of the mandatory charge given service is typically a single food drop rather than ongoing table service. Regularly praised for cleanliness and family-friendly discount nights ($5 kids movies and meals).

name: Lubbock
description: Flix Brewhouse's Lubbock location, a former Alamo Drafthouse space that draws frequent comparisons to its predecessor in reviews — some favorable, some not. Seats do not recline, which a couple of reviewers note is awkward with the fixed dining tables. Full bar and food are ordered via QR code/app and delivered to your seat by staff, with the standard automatic 18%+ gratuity. Recent reviews are more critical than most Flix locations, citing weaker cocktails and popcorn than the previous operator; other recent visitors report attentive, name-recognized server service and a solid overall experience — opinion here is unusually split for the chain.

name: Madison
description: Flix Brewhouse's Madison location, praised consistently for a rotating seasonal house-brewed beer list and a full kitchen menu delivered to reserved recliner seating. Ordering runs through a QR code or server, with the chain's automatic 18%+ gratuity added regardless. The most common critique is that food and drink prices feel high for the convenience of in-seat service, and a couple of reviewers wish for more classic concession-stand options (hot dogs, plain nachos) alongside the fuller menu.

name: Mansfield
description: Flix Brewhouse's Mansfield location in the Dallas-Fort Worth area. Full bar, reserved seating, and food ordered via QR code or server with the standard automatic 18%+ gratuity. This location's reviews skew more critical than most in the chain — recurring complaints include slow service, order mix-ups, one unauthorized-charge dispute, and a case where a bartender declined a second alcoholic drink without a food order. Other visitors report clean facilities and strong food quality, so the experience appears to vary more by visit than at other Flix locations.

name: Oklahoma City
description: Flix Brewhouse's Oklahoma City location, often compared favorably by reviewers to Studio Movie Grill as a similar dine-in alternative. Reserved recliner seating with chair-side food and drink service via QR code or server, house-brewed and specialty beers, and the chain's automatic 18%+ gratuity. Reviews are consistently positive, highlighting friendly bartenders, ample on-site parking, bottomless popcorn and fountain drinks, and a rewards program that brings regulars back for older-movie screenings.

name: Round Rock
description: Flix Brewhouse's original Round Rock location near Austin, open since 2011 and one of the chain's longest-running theaters. Full house brewery and bar, reserved recliner seating with individual pull-out tables, and food/drinks ordered via QR code or server with an automatic 18%+ gratuity. Long-time regulars are generally positive but flag a couple of recent friction points, including a policy limiting additional alcohol orders without a food purchase and pull-out tables some reviewers find too high and glare-prone when seats are reclined. Weekday discount ticket pricing (as low as $6) comes up often.

name: San Antonio
description: Flix Brewhouse's San Antonio location, popular enough that reviewers note you can visit just for the restaurant/bar without seeing a movie. Full bar and house-brewed beer, reserved seating (recliners in some auditoriums), and food ordered via QR code or through a server, with the standard automatic 18%+ gratuity disclosed up front. Reviews are strongly positive on food quality and service, with the most common critique being that self-service ordering can be finicky on some phones and that dessert options have been trimmed back recently.
